behavioral.question: Describe a time when a project you were working on failed. How did you handle it and what did you learn?
Tell me about a time you had a conflict with a team member who was not contributing. How did you resolve it?
Imagine you discover a safety flaw in a design right before the deadline. What do you do?
Describe a situation where you faced a significant setback. How did you bounce back?
Tell me about a time you had to lead a team through a difficult challenge.
How do you handle situations where you and your teammates have different opinions on a technical approach?
Describe a time you realized you made a mistake that impacted your team. How did you address it?
Tell me about a time you had to work with someone whose working style was completely different from yours.
You are aware that a teammate is using unauthorized resources for a project. How do you handle this?
Describe a time when you had to learn a complex concept quickly to meet a project deadline.
Tell me about a time you had to compromise to achieve a team goal.
Describe a situation where you received negative feedback on your work. How did you react?
Tell me about a time you had to mediate a dispute between two other team members.
Imagine your team is falling behind schedule due to unforeseen technical issues. What steps do you take?
Describe a time you had to make a decision without having all the necessary information.
Tell me about a time you took the initiative to improve a team process.
You are asked to cut corners on a project to save costs, but it might compromise quality. What do you do?
Describe a time you had to adapt to a sudden change in project requirements.
Tell me about a time you had to motivate a team member who was struggling.
Describe a situation where your initial design failed during testing. What was your next step?
Tell me about a time you had to communicate a difficult technical concept to a non-technical team member.
How do you prioritize tasks when working on multiple projects with conflicting deadlines?
Describe a time you had to stand your ground on an engineering decision you believed was right.
Tell me about a time you had to work with limited resources or budget.
You find out a competitor has patented a design very similar to what your team is working on. What do you do?
Describe a time you had to step into a leadership role unexpectedly.
Tell me about a time you had to troubleshoot a problem that seemed unsolvable at first.
Describe a situation where you had to balance academic integrity with the pressure to succeed.
Tell me about a time you had to collaborate with a multidisciplinary team.
Describe a time you had to manage a difficult stakeholder or client.
Tell me about a time you had to sacrifice your own ideas for the benefit of the team.
Describe a situation where you had to navigate a cultural or communication barrier within a team.
Tell me about a time you had to handle a sudden crisis during a project execution.
Describe a time you had to give constructive criticism to a peer.

Tell us about a passion or strong interest of yours. How (and when) did you become involved in this interest and for how long have you been involved? What have you learned about yourself from this interest? How will you apply this knowledge as a student at the University of Waterloo?

Briefly describe a group, organization, or community that you have been involved in, are a member of, and/or have contributed to. What contributions have you made as a member of this group? Were you able to lead, influence others, and/or influence decisions for the good of the group? How has your involvement helped make this community better?

Describe a situation where you were treated unfairly or witnessed someone else being treated unfairly. What did you do at the time and why? Would you do anything differently if the same situation occurred today? Has this event impacted or changed who you are now and if so, how?
What experience(s) inside or outside of the classroom motivated you to apply to your chosen engineering program?

Briefly introduce yourself and tell us about a time where you faced a challenge in your studies or in another part of your life and how you confronted this challenge. How has confronting this challenge prepared you for studying engineering at university?
Describe an experience that taught you something, allowed you to grow, and built your skills.
Choose between teamwork, inclusivity, and community building. Describe an experience that you had in the past two years that enabled you to develop that characteristic.
Tell us about an assignment or project that you are very proud of. What about this assignment stands out to you? Did you face any challenges and how did you handle them?

Imagine that you are preparing for a very important test that all students your age must take. You have spent many days studying, but are having a hard time remembering the material. A friend suggests asking classmates for advice. Another friend suggests hiring a tutor. A third friend says you should keep studying. What would you do and why would that work best for you?
What are three words that describe who you are as a student? Explain why you chose each word and how they reflect your approach to learning and collaboration.
Tell me about your biggest strength and your biggest weakness. How do these impact your approach to teamwork and problem-solving in engineering contexts?

problem_solving.question: Estimate the number of tennis balls that can fit into a standard school bus.
How would you design an experiment to test the durability of a new composite material for aircraft wings?
You have 8 identical-looking spheres, but one is slightly heavier. Using a balance scale only twice, how do you find it?
Estimate the total volume of water required to fill all the swimming pools in Toronto.
How would you design a system to automatically sort different types of plastics in a recycling facility?
Estimate the number of smartphones currently in use in Canada.
You have two ropes that each take exactly 60 minutes to burn, but they burn at uneven rates. How do you measure 45 minutes?
How would you design an experiment to determine the optimal angle for solar panels in Waterloo during winter?
Estimate the total mass of all the vehicles crossing the Ambassador Bridge in a single day.
You are in a room with 3 switches, each controlling one of 3 lightbulbs in an adjacent room. You can only enter the adjacent room once. How do you match the switches to the bulbs?
How would you design a test to evaluate the aerodynamics of a new drone propeller design?
Estimate the number of piano tuners working in the Greater Toronto Area.
You have a 3-liter jug and a 5-liter jug, and an unlimited water supply. How do you measure exactly 4 liters?
How would you design an experiment to test the efficiency of a new regenerative braking system?
Estimate the total energy consumed by the University of Waterloo campus in one week.
You have 25 horses and a 5-lane track. What is the minimum number of races needed to find the 3 fastest horses without a stopwatch?
How would you design a water filtration system for a remote, off-grid community?
Estimate the number of cups of coffee sold at Tim Hortons in Ontario every morning.
A farmer has a wolf, a goat, and a cabbage, and needs to cross a river in a boat that only holds himself and one item. How does he do it without anything being eaten?
How would you design an experiment to test the thermal insulation properties of a new spacesuit material?
Estimate the total length of all the subway tracks in the TTC network.

You have 10 bags of coins. One bag contains counterfeit coins that weigh 9 grams each, while genuine coins weigh 10 grams. You have a digital scale and can only take one reading. How do you find the counterfeit bag?
How would you design a smart traffic light system to minimize congestion at a busy intersection?
Estimate the number of leaves on a mature maple tree in autumn.
There are 3 boxes: one with apples, one with oranges, and one with both. All are labeled incorrectly. By picking just one fruit from one box, how can you correctly label all boxes?
How would you design an experiment to test the structural integrity of a 3D-printed concrete bridge?
Estimate the total amount of data generated by all UofT students in a single day.
You are standing at a crossroads. One path leads to safety, the other to doom. There are two guards: one always lies, one always tells the truth. You can ask one question. What do you ask?
How would you design a wearable device to continuously monitor a patient's blood glucose levels non-invasively?
Estimate the number of flights taking off from Pearson International Airport in a year.
You have a 10x10 grid of squares. How many total squares of any size are there?
How would you design an experiment to test the battery life of a new electric vehicle under extreme cold conditions?
Estimate the total weight of the CN Tower.

As part of a sustainability committee, you are deciding where to install a limited number of bike-share stations on campus. What three variables would you prioritize, and how would they shape your final decision?
Think of a difficult math or logic problem that comes to mind. Walk through how you approached the problem and arrived at your solution.
Describe how you designed and implemented a system, activity or thing in your personal, academic or work life.
Describe a 3-step process you would use to determine how many elementary schools there are in a city of 5 million people. Explain your assumptions and reasoning at each step.

You want to determine if a new material created for solar panels increases the amount of energy that can be captured. You have acquired 15 panels of different sizes manufactured with different materials including the new material. What are the 3 most important variables to address in your experiment? How would you incorporate those variables in your experimental design?

What is your primary goal for attending the University of Waterloo? Have you explored, been exposed to, or have experience in the field you plan to pursue and if so, how? Did you turn to anyone for advice in exploring alternative options or backup plans for your goal and, if so, how did this person help you?

Describe 2 qualities that you feel would make you a good candidate for Engineering at the University of Toronto.
Please tell us a little bit about yourself and specifically what strengths you have which will help you to be successful in the engineering program at the University of Toronto.
Tell us about your education goals, your interest in your chosen program(s), and reasons for choosing to apply to the University of Waterloo.
